disclaimer: Availability, pricing and laws change frequently and vary within regions. This is general orientation, not legal or financial advice — always verify on the official pricing page and with local sources.

regions.name: India
availability: Nearly all major AI, cloud and dev services are available; a few launch features later in India.
Student verification (GitHub Student Pack, education discounts) works with Indian institutions.
Some international plans add taxes at checkout instead of the listed price.

privacy.note: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act is being phased in — if you collect user data, keep collection minimal and disclose it clearly.

payments: UPI rules everyday payments, but most global services bill by card — keep an international-enabled card (Visa/Mastercard) ready.
Recurring foreign card charges may trigger OTP verification; watch for failed renewals on free trials.

regions.name: United States
availability: Almost everything launches here first — the widest availability of AI tools and free tiers.
Listed prices usually exclude sales tax, added at checkout by state.

privacy.law: No single federal law (CCPA/CPRA in California + state laws)
privacy.note: Privacy rights depend on your state — California, Virginia, Colorado and others have their own consumer privacy acts.

payments: Stripe, PayPal and every major processor work fully — the easiest place to sell from.

regions.name: United Kingdom
availability: Full availability of major platforms; UK pricing often shown with VAT included.

privacy.note: The UK kept GDPR-style rules after Brexit — registration with the ICO may be required if you process personal data.

payments: Faster Payments, Stripe and PayPal all work smoothly; VAT (20%) is usually added at checkout.

regions.name: European Union
availability: Major services are available, but AI features sometimes arrive later while meeting EU rules.
Consumer purchases include a 14-day withdrawal right on most digital subscriptions.

privacy.note: The strictest privacy regime in the world: if you run a site or service collecting EU users' data, you need a privacy policy, consent for cookies and a lawful basis.

payments: SEPA transfers are cheap; cards work everywhere; prices must be shown with VAT for consumers.

regions.name: Germany
availability: Everything major is available; Germany has excellent cheap VPS and dedicated-server providers.

privacy.note: Enforcement is notably strict — and German websites legally need an Impressum (legal notice) with your identity and address.

payments: SEPA direct debit is popular; some services accept it where cards fail.

regions.name: Canada
availability: Near-full availability of global services; pricing shown in USD more often than CAD.

privacy.note: Federal privacy law covers commercial data handling; Quebec's Law 25 adds stricter consent and privacy-officer requirements.

payments: GST/HST may be added at checkout; all major processors work.

regions.name: Australia
availability: Full availability of major platforms; some US-only offers (like certain cloud regions) differ.

privacy.note: Australian Privacy Principles apply to businesses handling personal data — the small-business exemption covers many hobby projects.

payments: GST 10% added for most digital purchases; all major processors work.

regions.name: Brazil
availability: Major AI and cloud services are available; Pix-native local alternatives are everywhere.
Imported hardware (GPUs, mini-PCs) carries high import duties — factor that into self-hosting plans.

privacy.note: Brazil's data-protection law mirrors GDPR closely — lawful basis, privacy policy and data-subject rights apply.

payments: Pix makes local payments instant and free; international card charges can still be declined — installments (parcelado) are common locally.

regions.name: Nigeria
availability: Most global services are accessible; the bigger barrier is payment, not availability.
Card limits and FX restrictions can block USD subscriptions — many devs use virtual dollar cards or Payoneer.

privacy.note: Applies to controllers processing Nigerian residents' data — registration duties exist for larger processors.

payments: Paystack and Flutterwave make local charging easy; paying international vendors is the hard direction.

regions.name: Kenya
availability: Global services are generally accessible; M-Pesa-based local platforms dominate domestic payments.

privacy.note: Registration with the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner is required for data controllers/processors.

payments: M-Pesa is king locally; international subscriptions need a card or mobile-linked services.

regions.name: South Africa
availability: Major services available; load-shedding (scheduled power cuts) matters if you self-host at home — budget a UPS.

privacy.note: Protection of Personal Information Act applies to anyone processing South African residents' data.

payments: Cards work for most international services; check FX fees on subscriptions.

regions.name: Singapore
availability: Excellent availability and connectivity; many cloud providers price Singapore as a premium region — compare region pricing.

privacy.note: Applies to organisations collecting personal data in Singapore — consent and purpose limitation are core rules.

payments: Everything works; GST (9%) is applied to imported digital services.

regions.name: Indonesia
availability: Major platforms are available; USD prices feel large in rupiah — use free tiers aggressively.

privacy.note: Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law is in force with GDPR-style consent requirements.

payments: GoPay/OVO/DANA dominate locally; international subscriptions need a card or virtual payment methods.

regions.name: Philippines
availability: Strong availability — the Philippines is a global freelancing hub, so most tools support it well.

privacy.note: NPC registration applies to some data processors; basic consent and notice rules for websites.

payments: GCash dominates locally; international subscriptions work with major cards.

regions.name: Pakistan
availability: Services are mostly accessible; PayPal is not available — Payoneer and Wise are common workarounds for receiving payments.

privacy.note: Comprehensive personal-data legislation has been in the works; follow current guidance before launching a data-heavy product.

payments: International card acceptance is limited; Debit cards with international activation are the common path.

regions.name: Bangladesh
availability: Major platforms accessible; bKash and local cards (dual-currency endorsement) unlock international payments.

privacy.note: A dedicated data-protection law has been drafted; sectoral rules (like ICT Act) currently apply.

payments: Dual-currency cards are required for international subscriptions; freelance payouts usually flow through Payoneer.

regions.name: United Arab Emirates
availability: Excellent availability; UAE is a regional hub with local cloud regions from major providers.

privacy.note: The Personal Data Protection Law regulates processing of UAE residents' data; free zones may have separate regimes (e.g. DIFC).

payments: Cards and local processors work fully; VAT is 5%.

regions.name: Japan
availability: Full availability of major platforms; Japanese-localized pricing is common for consumer services.

privacy.note: The Act on the Protection of Personal Information requires purpose specification and handling duties for personal data.

payments: Credit cards, plus convenience-store (konbini) and bank-transfer payment options on local services.
